payload.name: Indian Railway Catering & Tourism Corporation Ltd

business_snapshot.title: Business Snapshot & Operations Overview
business_snapshot.text: Indian Railway Catering & Tourism Corporation Ltd (IRCTC) operates across four primary business segments: Internet Ticketing, Catering, Rail Neer, and Tourism. In FY 2025-26, Internet Ticketing generated ₹1,536 crore (7.66% YoY growth), holding an 88.74% share of online bookings, which further expanded to 88.92% with ₹361 crore revenue and >80% EBITDA margins in Q1 FY27. Catering registered ₹2,399 crore in FY26 (+12.88% YoY), serving over 63 crore meals annually across >1,450 trains via >800 kitchens, and hit ₹732 crore in Q1 FY27 (+33.82% YoY). Rail Neer achieved ₹407 crore revenue in FY26 (+20.65% profit growth) with 17.77 lakh bottles/day installed capacity. Tourism reached ₹890 crore (+19.49% YoY). Co-branded credit card programs contributed ₹52.33 crore.

financial_snapshot.title: Financial Snapshot & Historical Performance
financial_snapshot.text: For FY 2025-26, IRCTC reported Revenue from Operations of ₹5,214.86 crore (+11.55% YoY), EBITDA of ₹1,926.12 crore (+8.30% YoY), PBT of ₹1,875.08 crore, and PAT of ₹1,393.37 crore. Net Profit Margin stood at 26.72% and EBITDA margin at 35.18%. Quarter-on-quarter actuals indicate revenue growth momentum from ₹1,225 crore in Dec 2024 to ₹1,449 crore in Dec 2025 (+18% YoY) and ₹1,333 crore in Sep 2026 (+16% YoY). However, Operating Profit Margins compressed from peak levels of 35% in Sep 2025 to 27% in Mar 2026 and 31% in Sep 2026. Net Profit peaked at ₹394 crore in Dec 2025 before declining to ₹264 crore in Sep 2026.

trajectory.title: Revenue & Margin Trajectory Analysis
trajectory.text: IRCTC maintains robust top-line growth driven by passenger volume expansion and Catering scale. Revenue growth sustained double-digit strength across recent quarters (+18% in Dec 2025, +18% in Jun 2026, +16% in Sep 2026). However, profitability trajectory shows margin pressure: Q1 FY27 EBITDA dropped 2.77% YoY to ₹386 crore with EBITDA margins contracting to 28.17%. Deceleration in profit was impacted by rising HR expenses and input cost inflation in plastic resin. Internet Ticketing volume remained strong at 14.58 lakh daily tickets (13.27 crore total tickets in Q1 FY27), while UPI share in ticket payments expanded from 48.72% in Jun 2025 to 51.22% in Q1 FY27.

balance_sheet.title: Balance Sheet & Capital Structure
balance_sheet.text: IRCTC operates a debt-light balance sheet with a Debt-to-Equity ratio of 0.02 and total net worth of ₹4,308.38 crore as of March 31, 2026. Current Ratio stands comfortably at 2.15, supported by an Interest Coverage Ratio of 57.92. Working capital metrics reveal Debtors' Turnover at 126.74 days. A significant concentration of receivables exists, with total trade receivables from Railways and Government standing at ₹1,870.29 crore, including ₹389.89 crore outstanding for over 3 years and ₹35.80 crore defaulted. Furthermore, IRCTC holds ₹86,375.96 lakhs (₹863.76 crore) in rolling deposits with the Ministry of Railways for ticket bookings.

cash_quality.title: Cash Quality, Governance & Legal Contingencies
cash_quality.text: Audit disclosures highlight significant statutory and tax contingencies: total unacknowledged tax/legal claims equal ₹16,630.78 lakhs (including Service Tax ₹8,561.26 lakhs and GST ₹3,100.42 lakhs). Additionally, a National Anti-Profiteering Authority notice of ₹5,041.44 lakhs regarding Rail Neer GST benefit pass-through is pending before GSTAT. Advance rulings filed for GST applicability on ₹33,595 lakhs received from Ministry of Railways remain pending. Four Rail Neer DCOs withheld GST input tax credit data worth ₹1,847.30 lakhs. Governance risk is underscored by non-compliance with Board composition rules under Companies Act, SEBI LODR, and DPE Guidelines due to missing Independent Directors.

narrative_vs_numbers.title: Narrative vs. Operational Numbers
narrative_vs_numbers.text: While management highlighted continuous expansion in Catering revenue (+33.82% in Q1 FY27) and daily E-catering meals growth (reaching 1.6 to 1.69 lakh meals/day), operating margins faced headwind pressures not fully reflected in top-line commentary. Operating Profit Margin compressed to 28.17% in Q1 FY27. This was driven by a ₹20 crore incremental HR expense impact (including gratuity cap increases) and a 30% surge in raw plastic resin prices linked to the West Asia crisis, which squeezed Rail Neer segment margins down from 14-15% to 10%.

guidance.title: Management Guidance & Growth Strategy
guidance.text: Management's forward strategy focuses on non-convenience ticketing monetization, Rail Neer capacity additions, and fintech expansion. Target is set to scale non-convenience fee revenue back toward ₹150 crore. Operational plant expansions include augmenting Ambernath (from 2 to 3 lakh bottles/day) and Danapur (from 1 to 2 lakh bottles/day), alongside new plants in Prayagraj, Mysore, Ranchi, and Bhagalpur. Infrastructure investments include ₹150 crore allocated for NGET IT refresh and site modernization. Final application for the iPay payment aggregator license was submitted to RBI on August 4, 2026.

bull_vs_bear.title: Bull vs. Bear Thesis Summary
bull_vs_bear.text: Bull Case: IRCTC commands a near-monopoly in online ticketing (88.92% market share) producing >80% EBITDA margins. Expanding catering scale (>63 crore meals/year), high return ratios (ROCE 46.1%, ROE 34.7%), low debt (0.02 D/E), and iPay fintech licensing offer long-term compounding strength. Bear Case: High receivables risk with ₹1,870.29 crore tied up in Railways/Government (₹389.89 crore >3 years), ongoing margin drag from input costs and HR expenses, corporate governance non-compliance on Independent Directors, and significant pending tax/anti-profiteering litigations exceeding ₹500 crore.

rows.delivered: Land allotted in Prayagraj and Mysore; confirmation received for Ranchi. Completion timeline extends beyond FY 26-27.

business_snapshot.title: Business Snapshot
business_snapshot.text: ETERNAL operates across four key business segments: Food delivery (Zomato), Quick commerce (Blinkit), Going-out (District), and B2B supplies (Hyperpure) (Annual Report Annual Report 2026, p. 55). Quick commerce has transitioned to an inventory model (1P) where 90-95% of SKUs are 1P, recognizing the full monetary value of goods sold in revenue (Concall Oct 2026, p. 5; Annual Report Annual Report 2026, p. 55). In Q2FY27, B2C NOV reached INR 35,644 crore (+54% YoY), driven by Quick Commerce NOV of INR 20,940 crore (+79.3% YoY) with 2,751 stores, and Food Delivery NOV of INR 11,445 crore (+21.5% YoY) (Concall Oct 2026, p. 7). District NOV reached INR 3,259 crore, while Hyperpure LFL revenue grew 22.7% to INR 1,154 crore (Concall Oct 2026, p. 7).

financial_snapshot.title: Financial Snapshot
financial_snapshot.text: For Sep 2026 (Q2FY27), ETERNAL reported Sales of Rs 24,138 Cr (+78% YoY) and Operating Profit of Rs 752 Cr with an OPM of 3.1%. Consolidated Profit Before Tax stood at Rs 323 Cr, but after a high tax rate of 61%, Net Profit was Rs 125 Cr (EPS Rs 0.13). For FY26, consolidated revenue from operations grew 169% YoY to INR 54,364 crore from INR 20,243 crore in FY25 (Annual Report Annual Report 2026, p. 56). FY26 Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA reached INR 1,189 crore, and reported EBITDA was INR 1,208 crore (Annual Report Annual Report 2026, p. 56). Annual PAT fell to INR 366 crore in FY26 from INR 527 crore in FY25 due to elevated depreciation in quick commerce (Annual Report Annual Report 2026, p. 56).

trajectory.title: Trajectory & Performance Trend
trajectory.text: Quarterly sales have expanded dramatically from Rs 5,405 Cr in Dec 2024 to Rs 24,138 Cr in Sep 2026, backed by three consecutive quarters of triple-digit YoY top-line expansion (+202% in Dec 2025, +196% in Mar 2026, +182% in Jun 2026). Operating profit expanded from Rs 162 Cr (3.0% OPM) in Dec 2024 to Rs 752 Cr (3.1% OPM) in Sep 2026. Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA grew 197% YoY in Q2FY27 to INR 666 crore (Concall Oct 2026, p. 7). EBITDA margins in food delivery remained steady at 5.5% of NOV (INR 627 crore profit) in Q2FY27, while Blinkit EBITDA margin rose to 0.9% of NOV (INR 184 crore profit) (Concall Oct 2026, p. 7).

balance_sheet.title: Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation
balance_sheet.text: As of March 31, 2026, total consolidated assets stood at INR 40,736 crore against total liabilities of INR 9,763 crore (Annual Report Annual Report 2026, p. 201). The cash balance ended at INR 16,475 crore as of September 30, 2026, declining by INR 1,813 crore in Q2FY27 due to seasonal working capital expansion (Concall Oct 2026, p. 11). Out of INR 8,436.12 crore net QIP proceeds, INR 5,599.08 crore has been cumulatively utilized, leaving INR 2,837.04 crore unutilized (Annual Report Annual Report 2026, p. 65). Investments in associates/other entities measured at FVTOCI stand at INR 1,781 crore (Annual Report Annual Report 2026, p. 191). Steady-state quick commerce metrics project dark store capex at INR 2.5 crore (Concall Jul 2026, p. 6).

cash_quality.title: Cash Flow Quality & Working Capital
cash_quality.text: For FY26, operating cash flow (CFO) was INR 632 crore, net cash generated from investing activities was INR 536 crore, and net cash used in financing activities was INR 842 crore (Annual Report Annual Report 2026, p. 205). In Q1FY27, net working capital was INR 2,545 crore (~14 days of annualized NOV) (Concall Jul 2026, p. 5). Quick commerce inventory losses stand at 1.8% of NOV due to perishables shrinkage and transit damage (Concall Jul 2026, p. 6). Other Income heavily aids quarterly profitability, coming in at Rs 351 Cr in Sep 2026 against a PBT of Rs 323 Cr, reflecting that underlying pre-tax profits are dependent on non-operating income.

narrative_vs_numbers.title: Narrative vs. Numbers
narrative_vs_numbers.text: Management highlights hyper-growth and scaling profit margins, with B2C NOV hitting INR 35,644 crore in Q2FY27 and Adjusted EBITDA surging 197% YoY to INR 666 crore (Concall Oct 2026, p. 7). However, standard accounting quarterly Net Profit fluctuates sharply due to heavy taxation (61% tax rate in Sep 2026 and 66% in Jun 2026) and rising quarterly depreciation (Rs 625 Cr in Sep 2026 vs Rs 247 Cr in Dec 2024). Additionally, cash balance fell by INR 1,813 crore in Q2FY27 to INR 16,475 crore due to working capital commitments (Concall Oct 2026, p. 11). Tax and legal contingencies remain notable with unresolved GST demand orders/SCNs exceeding INR 434 crore (Concall Oct 2026, p. 32).

bull_vs_bear.text:
Bull Case: Rapid scale in Quick Commerce with Blinkit NOV up 79.3% YoY to INR 20,940 crore and store count reaching 2,751 (Concall Oct 2026, p. 7). Steady-state target dark store economics point to 41.7% pre-tax ROCE and INR 11 lakh NOV per store per day (Concall Jul 2026, p. 6). Food delivery maintains solid profitability with 5.5% EBITDA margin of NOV (Concall Oct 2026, p. 7).

business_snapshot.title: Business Snapshot
business_snapshot.text: Avenue Supermarts Ltd (DMart) operated 500 stores across 15 States, 1 Union Territory, and NCR in FY26, adding 85 new stores to reach 20.58 mn sq. ft. of retail area {"doc": "Annual Report Annual Report 2026", "period": null, "page": "3"}. By H1/27, total store count reached 518 stores, including 132 in Maharashtra, 77 in Gujarat, 53 in Karnataka, 48 in Telangana, and 47 in Andhra Pradesh {"doc": "Concall Jul 2026", "period": "H1/27", "page": "6"}. Total retail business area expanded to 21.4 mn sq ft in Q2/27 {"doc": "Concall Oct 2026", "period": "Q2/27", "page": "10"}. DMart Ready expanded its presence to 19 cities in H1/27 {"doc": "Concall Oct 2026", "period": "H1/27", "page": "7"}. The product sales mix in H1/27 comprised Foods at 57.01%, Non-Foods (FMCG) at 19.65%, and General Merchandise & Apparel at 23.34% {"doc": "Concall Aug 2026", "period": "H1/27", "page": "5"}.

financial_snapshot.title: Financial Snapshot
financial_snapshot.text: For FY26, Revenue from Operations reached INR 66,968 crore, with EBITDA at INR 5,255 crore (7.8% margin) and PAT at INR 3,224 crore (4.8% margin) {"doc": "Concall Aug 2026", "period": "FY26", "page": "11"}. In H1/27, Revenue from Operations was INR 37,550 crore, EBITDA was INR 2,298 crore (6.1% margin), and PAT stood at INR 1,739 crore (4.6% margin) {"doc": "Concall Oct 2026", "period": "H1/27", "page": "11"}. Standardized quarterly actuals show sales rising from Rs 15,973 Cr in Dec 2024 to Rs 19,644 Cr in Sep 2026, while quarterly Net Profit increased from Rs 724 Cr to Rs 743 Cr over the same period. trajectory.title: Growth Trajectory & Revenue Dynamics
trajectory.text: Revenue growth maintained positive momentum, with YoY sales growth ranging between +13% (Dec 2025) and +19% (Mar 2026), reaching +18% in Sep 2026 at Rs 19,644 Cr. Like-For-Like (LFL) growth (>24 months) improved to 9.5% in Q2/27 from 6.8% in Q2/26, after dipping to 5.5% in Q1/27 {"doc": "Concall Aug 2026", "period": "Q2/27", "page": "10"}. Annualized revenue per sq ft of retail business area was INR 8,741 in Q2/27 compared to INR 8,692 in Q2/26 {"doc": "Concall Jul 2026", "period": "Q2/27", "page": "10"}. Total bill cuts grew to 11.1 crore in Q2/27 from 9.7 crore in Q2/26 {"doc": "Concall Aug 2026", "period": "Q2/27", "page": "10"}. EBITDA margin contracted from 8.7% in FY23 to 7.8% in FY26 {"doc": "Concall Aug 2026", "period": "FY26", "page": "11"}.

balance_sheet.title: Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation
balance_sheet.text: Equity increased to INR 27,290 crore in H1/27 while Total Debt rose significantly to INR 4,079 crore, taking the Debt/Equity ratio to 0.15 compared to 0.03 in FY23 and 0.09 in FY26 {"doc": "Concall Jul 2026", "period": "H1/27", "page": "12"}. Inventory days expanded to 36.1 days in H1/27 from 28.8 days in FY23, while Days Payables stood at 6.8 days {"doc": "Concall Aug 2026", "period": "H1/27", "page": "12"}. Standalone inventory was Rs 5,630.44 crore as of March 31, 2026, with an allowance for shrinkage/slow-moving stock of Rs 70.08 crore and total annual shrinkage/damage of Rs 275.24 crore {"doc": "Annual Report Annual Report 2026", "period": "FY26", "page": "126"}. Capital commitments for sites under construction were Rs 5,238.65 crore {"doc": "Annual Report Annual Report 2026", "period": "FY26", "page": "174"}.

cash_quality.title: Cash Flow Quality & Asset Efficiency
cash_quality.text: Consolidated net cash flow from operations was INR 4,168 crore for FY26 and INR 2,298 crore for H1/27 {"doc": "Concall Aug 2026", "period": "H1/27", "page": "11"}. Standalone operating cash flow for FY26 stood at Rs 3,612.30 crore, while investing cash flow was negative Rs 4,425.08 crore due to ongoing store network expansion, and financing cash flow was Rs 350.35 crore {"doc": "Annual Report Annual Report 2026", "period": "FY26", "page": "137"}. Fixed asset turnover ratio dropped from 3.7 in FY23 to 3.2 in FY26 and 1.7 in H1/27 {"doc": "Concall Aug 2026", "period": "H1/27", "page": "12"}. narrative_vs_numbers.title: Narrative vs. Numbers Breakdown
narrative_vs_numbers.text: Management oversaw major leadership transitions in FY26, with Mr. Anshul Asawa taking over as MD & CEO from Mr. Ignatius Navil Noronha, and Ms. Kalpana Unadkat succeeding Mr. Chandrashekhar Bhave as Chairperson {"doc": "Annual Report Annual Report 2026", "period": "FY26", "page": "47"}. While store expansion accelerated to 518 stores by H1/27 {"doc": "Concall Oct 2026", "period": "H1/27", "page": "6"}, return metrics softened: Return on Net Worth fell from 16.8% in FY23 to 13.5% in FY26 and 6.6% in H1/27, while ROCE declined from 20.1% to 17.1% in FY26 and 8.1% in H1/27 {"doc": "Concall Aug 2026", "period": "H1/27", "page": "12"}. Furthermore, continuous operational losses in Avenue E-Commerce Limited (AEL) presented impairment risks against its Rs 1,488.11 crore carrying value {"doc": "Annual Report Annual Report 2026", "period": "FY26", "page": "126"}.

guidance.text: Primary source filings do not provide explicit numerical management guidance for future revenue or margin targets. The company continues its physical footprint expansion across core markets like Maharashtra (132 stores) and Gujarat (77 stores) while scaling DMart Ready presence across 19 cities {"doc": "Concall Jul 2026", "period": "H1/27", "page": "6"}, supported by CSR expenditure commitments of Rs 72.33 crore for FY26 {"doc": "Annual Report Annual Report 2026", "period": "FY26", "page": "174"}.

business_snapshot.title: Business Snapshot
business_snapshot.text: KPIT Technologies Ltd specializes in automotive and mobility engineering services. In FY26, total revenue reached USD 724.8 million (up 4.8% YoY in USD terms and 10.5% in INR terms). Geographic revenue distribution is led by Europe at 48.0%, the USA at 27.4%, and Rest of World at 24.6%. By industry vertical, Passenger Cars account for 79.0%, Commercial Vehicles 18.0%, and Others 3.0%. Practice areas are dominated by Feature Development & Integration (59.8%), followed by Architecture & Middleware (22.3%) and Cloud-Based Connected Services (17.9%). Fixed-price contracts represent over 70% of engagements. AI adoption spans over 9,000 platform users and 12,000 engineering agents, contributing roughly 9% of total revenues.

financial_snapshot.title: Financial Snapshot
financial_snapshot.text: KPIT trades at a Market Cap of Rs 15,133 Cr with a stock price of Rs 552, Book Value of Rs 134, and Stock P/E of 26.3. Return metrics are strong, with ROCE at 26.3% and ROE at 20.9%. Quarterly sales grew from Rs 1,478 Cr in Dec 2024 to Rs 1,691 Cr in Sep 2026, though YoY sales growth moderated from +18% to +6% over the period. Operating Profit Margin (OPM) compressed from 21% in Dec 2024/Mar 2025 to 15% in Jun 2026 and 16% in Sep 2026. Consequently, Net Profit fell from Rs 187 Cr in Dec 2024 (and Rs 245 Cr in Mar 2025) to Rs 121 Cr in Sep 2026, with EPS ending at Rs 4.40.

trajectory.title: Trajectory & Growth Trends
trajectory.text: Overall top-line growth slowed to 6.5% YoY and 1.0% QoQ in rupee terms (0.2% YoY and 0.5% QoQ in constant currency terms). Performance shows distinct segment divergence: Off-highway and Commercial grew significantly at 27% YoY and 17.6% QoQ, whereas Passenger Cars dropped by 8% YoY and 4% sequentially. Top-line expansion faced headwinds from program cancellations and expense reductions in top two client accounts, which represented a 13% impact on total revenue. Conversely, Products revenue showed strength, expanding 25% YoY and 5% QoQ.

balance_sheet.title: Balance Sheet & Financial Health
balance_sheet.text: KPIT maintains a conservative leverage profile with Long Term Debt to Equity at 4.0% and Total Debt to Equity at 13.1% in FY26. Cash and cash equivalents totaled Rs 14,268.6 million, representing 19.7% of total assets. Concall disclosures report net cash standing at approximately INR 6.2 billion. Capital commitments are Rs 62.74 million for PPE and Rs 85.76 million for intangible assets. Corporate guarantees issued on behalf of subsidiaries total Rs 545.03 million (KPIT GmbH) and Rs 283.96 million (KPIT Holding Inc.), with zero underlying borrowings drawn. Contingent tax liabilities stand at Rs 1.60 million across AY 2019–21.

cash_quality.title: Cash Flow & Capital Allocation
cash_quality.text: Net cash decreased to INR 6.2 billion due to key cash outflows: a dividend payment of INR 1.4 billion, an initial acquisition payment of ~INR 1 billion for Cymotive, and working capital expansion. Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) increased from 51 days to 53 days. Capital allocation included expanding group ownership in N-Dream AG to 90% and approving renegotiated consideration for Caresoft Engineering Solutions up to USD 157 million (including USD 15 million variable pay across 4 years). Outstanding bank guarantees in the routine course of business total Rs 6.49 million.

narrative_vs_numbers.title: Narrative vs Numbers
narrative_vs_numbers.text: Management highlights operational stability, citing EBITDA margin expansion from 17.2% to 17.8% (up 60 bps QoQ) due to product mix, alongside an annual FY26 EBITDA margin of 20.8%. However, quarterly actuals indicate margin pressure: OPM declined from 21% in Dec 2024 to 15% in Jun 2026 and 16% in Sep 2026, while Net Profit dropped from Rs 187 Cr to Rs 121 Cr over the same period. Additionally, management notes strong strategic positioning, but client concentration risks materialized via a 13% revenue drag from program cuts in the top two accounts.

guidance.title: Guidance & Outlook
guidance.text: Management expects H2 performance to outperform H1, with growth resuming in Q4. In Europe, supplier consolidation processes are anticipated to conclude meaningfully by the end of Q1 next year. Long term, KPIT has committed to becoming a net-zero organization by the end of the decade using EcoVoyage and science-based targets. Technology investments are planned to remain above 5% of revenue to support product innovation and execute fixed-price contracts (over 70% of new engagements).

bull_vs_bear.title: Bull vs Bear Case
bull_vs_bear.text: The Bull Case centers on rapid expansion in Off-highway & Commercial (+27% YoY), strong product revenue growth (+25% YoY), robust return ratios (ROCE 26.3%, ROE 20.9%), high fixed-price mix (>70%), and expanding AI integration (9% of revenue from AI-first projects). The Bear Case emphasizes sharp weakness in Passenger Cars (-8% YoY), significant client concentration risks (13% revenue loss from top 2 accounts), operating margin compression (OPM down to 16% in Sep 2026 from 21% in Dec 2024), rising DSO (53 days), and cash drains from M&A commitments such as Caresoft ($157M).

rows.promise: Expect H2 to be better than H1.
rows.delivered: Unverifiable from available quarterly actuals (actuals end at Sep 2026).

rows.promise: Expect growth in Q4.
Supplier consolidation process in Europe meaningfully concluded by the end of the first quarter next year.

business_snapshot.title: Business Snapshot
business_snapshot.text: CDSL is India's leading depository with an 80%+ market share in demat accounts, reaching 19.34 crore Beneficial Owner (BO) accounts and ₹89 lakh crore in demat custody by September 30, 2026. This expanded from 18.59 crore accounts in June 2026 and 18.01 crore accounts (₹77.18 lakh crore custody) as of March 31, 2026. Issuer count grew to 51,132 with 1,39,495 ISINs by Q2 FY27. Key subsidiaries include CDSL Ventures Limited (CVL, 100% owned), holding over 10.97 crore KYC records, CIRL (52% owned) holding 26.23 lakh insurance policies, and CCRL (54.25% owned). BSE Limited is the main promoter shareholder with a 15.00% stake.

financial_snapshot.title: Financial Snapshot
financial_snapshot.text: CDSL commands a market capitalization of ₹30,242 crore at a Stock P/E of 59.9 and face value of ₹10.0. Key return ratios are strong, with ROCE at 32.0% and ROE at 24.5%. In Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026), quarterly sales surged 24% YoY to ₹394 crore, operating profit reached ₹228 crore (58% OPM), and net profit reached ₹173 crore (EPS ₹8.32). Standalone Q2 FY27 operating income reached ₹339 crore, anchored by Annual Issuer Income of ₹129 crore and Transaction Charges of ₹68 crore. For H1 FY27, consolidated total income was ₹757.80 crore versus ₹636.53 crore YoY, yielding a net profit of ₹290.97 crore.

trajectory.title: Revenue & Earnings Trajectory
trajectory.text: Revenue growth accelerated meaningfully through 2026, recovering from -7% YoY in Mar 2025 (₹224 crore) and +1% in Jun 2025 to +17% in Mar 2026 (₹263 crore), +13% in Jun 2026 (₹293 crore), and +24% in Sep 2026 (₹394 crore). Operating margins rebounded from 44% in Mar 2026 and 47% in Jun 2026 back to 58% in Sep 2026. Net profit expanded from ₹80 crore in Mar 2026 to ₹118 crore in Jun 2026 and ₹173 crore in Sep 2026. Growth was fueled by high primary market activity, with IPO proceeds exceeding ₹86,500 crore ($9B+) in Q2 FY27, generating ₹24 crore in standalone IPO/CA income alongside Q2 margin pledge fees (₹6.19 crore) and e-voting income (₹22 crore).

balance_sheet.title: Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation
balance_sheet.text: CDSL holds zero debt with a book value of ₹94.9 per share and dividend yield of 0.88%. Treasury policies remain conservative, avoiding direct equity mutual fund schemes and maintaining only 5% to 7% of its portfolio in ETFs. Standalone capital commitments for property, plant, and equipment were ₹2,145.00 lakh as of March 31, 2026. Related-party payments included dividends of ₹3,526.88 lakh paid to BSE Limited in FY26. Consolidated contingent liabilities stand at ₹710.46 lakh in bank guarantees, ₹253.76 lakh in tax claims, and ₹886.03 lakh in legal matters, with pending arbitration/civil cases of ₹42,417 lakh assessed as remote liability risk by management.

cash_quality.title: Cash Flow & Earnings Quality
cash_quality.text: Earnings quality is backed by strong operational cash flow of ₹43,072.69 lakh against standalone net profit of ₹46,820.95 lakh in FY26. Cash outflows for investing and financing were ₹(15,374.23) lakh and ₹(26,213.41) lakh, respectively. Receivables display strong collection trends, supported by a debtor provision reversal of ₹1.77 crore in Q2 FY27 following ₹2.22 crore provisioned in Q1 FY27. Standalone earnings are periodically elevated by dividend distributions from CVL, such as ₹39.50 crore received in Q1 FY27 (compared to ₹62 crore in Q1 FY26), which inflates standalone profitability relative to pure operational income.

narrative_vs_numbers.title: Narrative vs Numbers
narrative_vs_numbers.text: Management highlights CDSL's market dominance (+75 lakh BO accounts added in Q2 FY27 to reach 19.34 crore), which translates into robust consolidated revenues of ₹417.30 crore in Q2 FY27. However, subsidiary metrics reveal regulatory headwinds. For CVL, H1 FY27 revenue rose 20% to ₹99.91 crore, but PAT declined 12% to ₹23.74 crore due to KRA tariff reductions. In addition, associate entity India International Bullion Holding IFSC Limited posted a loss of ₹2,157 lakh in FY26, highlighting a drag from non-core infrastructure investments.

guidance.title: Guidance & Future Outlook
guidance.text: Regulatory pricing rules implemented on April 1, 2026 reduced KRA creation fees by 75% to ₹5 and fetch fees by 20% to ₹28. To partially cushion this impact, a Search API fee of ₹0.25 was introduced for un-fetched/un-modified PAN searches. CDSL is diversifying revenue streams through unlisted issuer fees (₹87 lakh) and application processing fees (₹2.2 crore in Q2 FY27), while CIRL expands insurance policy digitization across 49 partner insurers. Macro projections cited in the annual report foresee Indian real GDP growing 6.8% to 7.2% and non-food bank credit expanding ~10.5% in FY 2026-27.

bull_vs_bear.title: Bull vs Bear Case
bull_vs_bear.text: Bull Case: CDSL maintains an 80%+ market share with 19.34 crore BO accounts and ₹89 lakh crore in demat custody. Strong operating leverage generated a 58% OPM in Q2 FY27, buoyed by ₹68 crore in transaction fees, ₹129 crore in annual issuer fees, and elevated IPO market activity. Bear Case: Regulatory tariff cuts on KRA services squeezed CVL's H1 FY27 PAT by 12%. Profitability remains sensitive to capital market transaction volume fluctuations, while pending legal and arbitration claims of ₹42,417 lakh pose tail risks if liabilities crystallize.

business_snapshot.title: Business Overview & Scale
business_snapshot.text: Varun Beverages Ltd (VBL) operates as a major franchisee for PepsiCo, covering carbonated soft drinks (73.3% of Q3 CY2026 volume), packaged drinking water (21.9%), and juice-based drinks (4.8%) as per Concall Nov 2026. Annual sales volume reached 1,213.1 million cases in CY 2025 across 50 manufacturing facilities (38 in India, 12 international). Distribution spans over 4.2 million outlets, supported by over 1 million coolers and digital initiatives like the 'Bandhan' B2B app serving 0.5 million monthly active retailers. VBL continues international expansion, completing the Twizza merger with BevCo, commencing operations in Kenya with 'BOLT UP' and 'XTREME FIZZ', and securing an exclusive distribution deal with Mondelez in Zimbabwe.

financial_snapshot.title: Quarterly Financial Overview
financial_snapshot.text: In Sep 2026 (Q3 CY2026), revenue from operations grew 33.2% YoY to Rs. 6,608 Cr (Rs. 66,075.6 million), while Net Profit rose 13.5% YoY to Rs. 831 Cr. Consolidated sales volume grew 28.7% (22.5% in India, 39.9% internationally). Operating profit reached Rs. 1,424 Cr with an OPM of 22% (EBITDA margin at 21.6%). Gross margins moderated by 334 bps YoY to 53.1%, driven by ~300 bps of pressure from elevated packaging material costs (preforms, shrink films, closures, cans) and a 100 bps impact from non-beverage COGS in India. A 16% increase in sugar prices was largely offset by expanding low/no-sugar products to 88% of the Indian portfolio.

trajectory.title: Growth Trajectory & Seasonality
trajectory.text: VBL displays strong top-line seasonality, peaking in the June quarters. Sales reached Rs. 7,017 Cr in Jun 2025 and surged 21.8% YoY to Rs. 8,545 Cr in Jun 2026, delivering an OPM of 27% and Net Profit of Rs. 1,510 Cr. YoY revenue growth accelerated from -2% in Jun 2025 to +18% in Mar 2026, +22% in Jun 2026, and +33% in Sep 2026. Over 9M CY2026, revenue increased 23.3% to Rs. 218,146 million, EBITDA grew 19.9% to Rs. 52,746 million, and PAT grew 15.5% to Rs. 32,023 million, despite temporary cost pressure from international M&A debt and packaging inputs.

balance_sheet.title: Capital Structure & Balance Sheet Health
balance_sheet.text: VBL India remained net debt-free with free cash of ~Rs. 12,250 million, while consolidated net debt stood at ~Rs. 256 million as of December 31, 2025. CRISIL upgraded its long-term credit rating to CRISIL AAA/Stable. Net capitalised capex reached ~Rs. 45,000 million in CY 2025 for greenfield plants and brownfield expansions. Finance costs rose 53.5% and depreciation rose 34.5% in Q3 CY2026 due to the acquisition of Twizza in South Africa and related debt funding. Debtors turnover expanded from 11 days in CY 2024 to 18 days in CY 2025, reflecting higher modern trade mix in South Africa.

cash_quality.title: Cash Flow & Audit Integrity
cash_quality.text: VBL generated Net Operating Cash Flows of Rs. 35,093.14 million for CY 2025 against Net Revenue of Rs. 216,853.8 million and PAT of Rs. 30,620.4 million. Consolidated contingent liabilities as of December 31, 2025 totaled ~Rs. 3,104 million (including GST Rs. 424.19m, Customs Rs. 481.87m, Sales/Entry Tax Rs. 1,011.15m, and Income Tax Rs. 773.09m). Joint statutory auditors highlighted qualifications in the CARO report of the holding company under Clause (i)(c) and Clause (iii)(e). RoNW stood at 15.5% in CY 2025 compared to 15.7% in CY 2024.

narrative_vs_numbers.title: Narrative vs Quarterly Actuals
narrative_vs_numbers.text: Management highlighted strong volume growth of 28.7% and revenue expansion of 33.2% YoY in Q3 CY2026, which matches reported screener actuals showing Sales growing from Rs. 4,961 Cr in Sep 2025 to Rs. 6,608 Cr in Sep 2026 (+33% YoY). However, narrative flags around input cost headwinds are reflected in reported profitability: OPM moderated to 22% in Sep 2026 (down from 23% in Sep 2025 and 27% in Jun 2026). Interest costs jumped to Rs. 72 Cr in Sep 2026 (up from Rs. 47 Cr in Sep 2025) and depreciation rose to Rs. 420 Cr, matching concall statements regarding debt funding for the Twizza acquisition.

bull_vs_bear.title: Bull vs Bear Case
bull_vs_bear.text:
Bull Case: Rapid international expansion via Twizza merger in South Africa, entrance into Kenya ('BOLT UP', 'XTREME FIZZ'), and Mondelez distribution in Zimbabwe ($11m existing business). Strong volume execution (+28.7% Q3 CY2026) alongside backward integration via 25% rPET usage and shifting 88% of India portfolio to low/no sugar protects unit economics.

Bear Case: Gross margins under pressure (-334 bps YoY to 53.1% in Q3 CY2026) due to packaging cost inflation (~300 bps) and non-beverage COGS dilution. Capital expenditure and acquisition debt increased finance costs by 53.5% and depreciation by 34.5%, while CARO audit qualifications and expanding debtor days (18 days in CY2025) warrant scrutiny.
